title: The thank-you dinner
setting: A small izakaya on a Friday evening. Mai (Kimura-san at work) has invited her manager Tanaka-san out to thank him for last month, when her cat was sick and she had to take a week off work. She means to pay.

speakers.name: Mai
speakers.voice: female, late 20s, warm, a little shy

speakers.name: Tanaka-san
speakers.voice: male, 40s, calm and kind, polite office speech

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: tanaka-san, kyou wa oisogashii tokoro, arigatou gozaimasu.
lines.ja: 田中さん、今日はお忙しいところ、ありがとうございます。
lines.kana: たなかさん、きょうはおいそがしいところ、ありがとうございます。
lines.english: Tanaka-san, thank you for coming tonight when you're so busy.

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: iie. de, kyuu ni dou shita n desu ka?
lines.ja: いいえ。で、急にどうしたんですか？
lines.kana: いいえ。で、きゅうにどうしたんですか？
lines.english: Not at all. So what's all this, out of the blue?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: sengetsu wa, neko ga byouki de isshuukan mo shigoto o yasunde, hontou ni osewa ni narimashita. dakara, chanto orei o iitakute.
lines.ja: 先月は、猫が病気で一週間も仕事を休んで、本当にお世話になりました。だから、ちゃんとお礼を言いたくて。
lines.kana: せんげつは、ねこがびょうきでいっしゅうかんもしごとをやすんで、ほんとうにおせわになりました。だから、ちゃんとおれいをいいたくて。
lines.english: Last month my cat was sick and I took a whole week off work, and you really looked after me. So I wanted to thank you properly.

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: sorede gohan desu ka. sonna ni ki o tsukawanakute ii noni.
lines.ja: それでご飯ですか。そんなに気を遣わなくていいのに。
lines.kana: それでごはんですか。そんなにきをつかわなくていいのに。
lines.english: So that's what dinner is for. You didn't need to go to all that trouble.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: iie! kyou no gohan wa, watashi ni ogorasete kudasai.
lines.ja: いいえ！今日のご飯は、私におごらせてください。
lines.kana: いいえ！きょうのごはんは、わたしにおごらせてください。
lines.english: No, no! Please let me treat you to dinner tonight.

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: sou desu ka. jaa, kyou wa gochisou ni narimasu.
lines.ja: そうですか。じゃあ、今日はごちそうになります。
lines.kana: そうですか。じゃあ、きょうはごちそうになります。
lines.english: Is that so? Well then, tonight I'll let you treat me.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: a, biiru, mou nai desu ne. tsugi, nani nomimasu ka? watashi, tanomimasu ne.
lines.ja: あ、ビール、もうないですね。次、何飲みますか？私、頼みますね。
lines.kana: あ、ビール、もうないですね。つぎ、なにのみますか？わたし、たのみますね。
lines.english: Oh, your beer's finished. What would you like next? I'll order it.

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: kimura-san, sakki kara ki o tsukatte bakari desu ne. kyou wa shigoto ja nai n desu kara, keigo mo tsukawanakute ii desu yo.
lines.ja: 木村さん、さっきから気を遣ってばかりですね。今日は仕事じゃないんですから、敬語も使わなくていいですよ。
lines.kana: きむらさん、さっきからきをつかってばかりですね。きょうはしごとじゃないんですから、けいごもつかわなくていいですよ。
lines.english: Kimura-san, you've done nothing but fuss over me all evening. We're not at work tonight, so you don't need to be formal with me, either.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: e, demo, tanaka-san mo keigo tsukattemasu yo.
lines.ja: え、でも、田中さんも敬語使ってますよ。
lines.kana: え、でも、たなかさんもけいごつかってますよ。
lines.english: Huh? But you're being formal too, Tanaka-san.

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: a, hontou da. jaa, kimura-san, tsugi, nani nomu?
lines.ja: あ、本当だ。じゃあ、木村さん、次、何飲む？
lines.kana: あ、ほんとうだ。じゃあ、きむらさん、つぎ、なにのむ？
lines.english: Oh, you're right. Okay then... Kimura-san, what're you drinking next?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: muri desu! tanaka-san ni wa, keigo tsukawasete kudasai.
lines.ja: 無理です！田中さんには、敬語使わせてください。
lines.kana: むりです！たなかさんには、けいごつかわせてください。
lines.english: I can't! Please let me keep being polite with you.

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: wakarimashita. jaa, ki wa tsukawanaide kudasai ne.
lines.ja: わかりました。じゃあ、気は遣わないでくださいね。
lines.kana: わかりました。じゃあ、きはつかわないでくださいね。
lines.english: All right. But no more fussing over me, then.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: sorosoro kaerimashou ka. watashi, haratte kimasu ne.
lines.ja: そろそろ帰りましょうか。私、払ってきますね。
lines.kana: そろそろかえりましょうか。わたし、はらってきますね。
lines.english: Shall we call it a night? I'll go and pay.

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: aa, sore nara, mou harattemasu yo.
lines.ja: ああ、それなら、もう払ってますよ。
lines.kana: ああ、それなら、もうはらってますよ。

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: e! gochisou ni narimasu tte itta ja nai desu ka!
lines.ja: え！「ごちそうになります」って言ったじゃないですか！
lines.kana: え！「ごちそうになります」っていったじゃないですか！
lines.english: What? But you said you'd let me treat you!

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: orei nara, mou chanto itte moraimashita kara. minna no mendou o miru no wa, watashi no shigoto desu yo.
lines.ja: お礼なら、もうちゃんと言ってもらいましたから。みんなの面倒を見るのは、私の仕事ですよ。
lines.kana: おれいなら、もうちゃんといってもらいましたから。みんなのめんどうをみるのは、わたしのしごとですよ。
lines.english: You've already thanked me properly, and that's plenty. Looking after everyone is my job.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: itsumo osewa ni natte bakari desu ne. gochisou ni narimashita. ashita, mata chanto orei o iwasete kudasai ne.
lines.ja: いつもお世話になってばかりですね。ごちそうになりました。明日、またちゃんとお礼を言わせてくださいね。
lines.kana: いつもおせわになってばかりですね。ごちそうになりました。あした、またちゃんとおれいをいわせてくださいね。
lines.english: I'm always the one being looked after. Thank you for dinner. Let me thank you properly again tomorrow.

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: sore jaa, itsu made mo owarimasen yo. ki o tsukete kaette kudasai ne.
lines.ja: それじゃあ、いつまでも終わりませんよ。気をつけて帰ってくださいね。
lines.kana: それじゃあ、いつまでもおわりませんよ。きをつけてかえってくださいね。
lines.english: At that rate, it'll never end. Get home safely, okay?

choices.english: Tanaka-san takes Mai out to thank her for her hard work, and in the end she pays.
Mai takes Tanaka-san out to thank him and means to pay, but he has already paid the bill.
Mai takes Tanaka-san out to thank him, and they agree to split the bill.

questions.explanation: Line 3: Mai has invited Tanaka-san out because he looked after her last month, and she wants to thank him properly (chanto orei o iitakute). In line 5 she asks to pay (watashi ni ogorasete kudasai) and in line 6 he seems to agree (gochisou ni narimasu). But when she goes to pay, he has already done it (mou harattemasu yo, line 14), and she protests in line 15. A swaps their roles: Mai is the one saying thanks, and she never gets to pay. C: nobody suggests splitting the bill; Tanaka-san pays all of it.

questions.english: Your friend Yuki tells you: "Tanaka-san helped me with all of yesterday's work." Ask whether she thanked him properly, or remind her that she should.
questions.ja: 昨日の仕事、田中さんが全部手伝ってくれたんだ。
questions.kana: きのうのしごと、たなかさんがぜんぶてつだってくれたんだ。
questions.romaji: kinou no shigoto, tanaka-san ga zenbu tetsudatte kureta n da.
questions.answer: Talk about the thanking with orei o iu: chanto orei itta? (did you thank him properly?) or ato de orei iwanakya ne (you'll have to thank him later).

modelAnswers.ja: じゃあ、ちゃんとお礼言った？
modelAnswers.english: So did you thank him properly?

modelAnswers.romaji: yokatta ne. ato de chanto orei iwanakya ne.
modelAnswers.ja: よかったね。後でちゃんとお礼言わなきゃね。
modelAnswers.english: That's great. You'll need to thank him properly later.

questions.explanation: Saying thanks, as opposed to just feeling it, is orei o iu. Mai says chanto orei o iitakute (line 3) and ashita, mata chanto orei o iwasete kudasai ne (line 17), and Tanaka-san answers orei nara, mou chanto itte moraimashita (line 16). English 'thank' points to kansha suru, but kansha shita? asks whether she felt grateful, not whether she said it. orei o suru would mean giving something back, like the dinner Mai planned.

questions.english: Kenta's flatmate Sora meets you for the first time and is very formal with you. You're about the same age. Tell him he doesn't need to be formal.
questions.ja: はじめまして、ソラです。よろしくお願いします。
questions.kana: はじめまして、そらです。よろしくおねがいします。
questions.romaji: hajimemashite, sora desu. yoroshiku onegai shimasu.
questions.answer: Drop the formality with keigo o tsukau in the negative: keigo tsukawanakute ii yo.

modelAnswers.romaji: keigo tsukawanakute ii yo. yoroshiku ne.
modelAnswers.ja: 敬語使わなくていいよ。よろしくね。
modelAnswers.english: No need to be formal with me. Nice to meet you.

modelAnswers.romaji: a, keigo wa tsukawanakute ii desu yo.
modelAnswers.ja: あ、敬語は使わなくていいですよ。
modelAnswers.english: Oh, you don't need to speak formally with me.

questions.explanation: The everyday verb with keigo is tsukau: Tanaka-san says keigo mo tsukawanakute ii desu yo (line 8), Mai answers tanaka-san mo keigo tsukattemasu yo (line 9) and then asks keigo tsukawasete kudasai (line 11). keigo o hanasu, built like nihongo o hanasu, is the English speaker's version. Don't swap in ki: ki o tsukawanakute ii means 'don't go to any trouble'. Tanaka-san says both in the same breath in line 8.

questions.english: When Mai says she wanted to thank him properly, what does Tanaka-san say?
questions.ja: 「お礼を言いたくて」と聞いて、田中さんは何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: 「おれいをいいたくて」ときいて、たなかさんはなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: orei o iitakute to kiite, tanaka-san wa nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: You didn't need to be so careful.
choices.romaji: sonna ni ki o tsukenakute ii noni.

choices.english: You didn't need to be so formal.
choices.romaji: sonna ni keigo o tsukawanakute ii noni.

choices.english: You didn't need to go to all that trouble.
choices.romaji: sonna ni ki o tsukawanakute ii noni.

questions.explanation: Line 4: sorede gohan desu ka. sonna ni ki o tsukawanakute ii noni. A thank-you dinner is more trouble than he thinks she needed to go to, and ki o tsukau is going to trouble for someone. A, ki o tsukenakute, is ki o tsukeru (be careful), the phrase in Tanaka-san's last line, ki o tsukete kaette kudasai ne (get home safely). B shares tsukau too, but Tanaka-san only brings up keigo later in the evening (line 8), not here.

questions.english: At the start, Mai tells Tanaka-san "hontou ni osewa ni narimashita" about last month. What does she mean?
questions.ja: 木村さんの「本当にお世話になりました」は、どういう意味ですか？
questions.kana: きむらさんの「ほんとうにおせわになりました」は、どういういみですか？
questions.romaji: kimura-san no hontou ni osewa ni narimashita wa, dou iu imi desu ka?

choices.english: She's thanking him for all his help when she had to take a week off for her sick cat.
She's reminding him that she covered his work for a week while he was away.
She's thanking him for looking after her cat while it was sick.

questions.explanation: Line 3: neko ga byouki de isshuukan mo shigoto o yasunde, hontou ni osewa ni narimashita. With ni naru, Mai is on the receiving end: she was the one looked after, through the week she was off work. She says it again at the end, itsumo osewa ni natte bakari desu ne (line 17). B turns it around; the one who does the looking after says mendou o miru, as Tanaka-san does in line 16 (minna no mendou o miru no wa, watashi no shigoto desu yo). C reads osewa as literal pet care, but nothing in the scene says Tanaka-san minded the cat; Mai stayed home with it.

questions.english: Tanaka-san takes you out to lunch and says: "Today's on me, so order whatever you like." Accept his offer politely.
questions.ja: 今日は私がおごりますから、好きなもの頼んでくださいね。
questions.kana: きょうはわたしがおごりますから、すきなものたのんでくださいね。
questions.romaji: kyou wa watashi ga ogorimasu kara, suki na mono tanonde kudasai ne.
questions.answer: Accept the treat with gochisou ni narimasu: jaa, gochisou ni narimasu.

modelAnswers.romaji: arigatou gozaimasu. jaa, gochisou ni narimasu.
modelAnswers.ja: ありがとうございます。じゃあ、ごちそうになります。
modelAnswers.english: Thank you. Then I'll gladly let you treat me.

modelAnswers.romaji: ii n desu ka? jaa, kyou wa gochisou ni narimasu.
modelAnswers.ja: いいんですか？じゃあ、今日はごちそうになります。
modelAnswers.english: Are you sure? Then I'll let you treat me today.

questions.explanation: With ni naru you are the one being treated. That's how Tanaka-san accepts Mai's offer in line 6 (jaa, kyou wa gochisou ni narimasu), and Mai uses the past, gochisou ni narimashita, to thank him afterwards (line 17). The payer's verbs are ogoru and gochisou suru, like Mai's watashi ni ogorasete kudasai (line 5), so gochisou shimasu here would mean you're paying. The passive gochisou saremasu is heard but much less usual.

newWords.english: a week (isshuukan mo = a whole week)
